limitations: Running under WSL2: 'guest' memory is the VM's allocation, not the physical host's.
WSL2 returns freed guest memory to Windows lazily, and the Linux page cache counts toward the VM's footprint on the host; system-wide 'used' excludes cache.
Windows-side memory pressure is invisible from inside the guest.

host.wslconfig: absent (WSL2 defaults apply: half of host memory, all logical processors)

methodology: Detection metrics are reported under explicit names with their populations (overall_fault_detection_*, drift_detection_*).
Remediation lifecycle events are recorded per proposal and reconciled.
LLM text is validated claim by claim; the raw text and the counters are stored.
Configuration D includes the LLM explanation step (run 'main' did not), so its latency is not comparable with 'main'.
Resources are sampled by the process-tree sampler every 0.5 s; each invocation is a separate record.

overall_fault_detection.definition: Was an incident opened? Positives: every injected-fault scenario, all fault categories. Negatives: clean control batches. A scenario counts as detected when the monitoring run reports an incident, raised by any monitor.

overall_fault_detection_f1.ci_method: percentile bootstrap over scenarios, 2000 resamples, fixed seed

drift_detection.definition: Did the drift monitor flag a distribution change? Positives: only the covariate-drift scenarios (numerical shift F01, categorical shift F02, scaling error F04). Negatives: the same clean control batches. A scenario counts as detected only when the drift monitor itself triggers; an incident raised by another monitor does not count.

drift_detection_f1.ci_method: percentile bootstrap over scenarios, 2000 resamples, fixed seed

methods_compared.note: same population as drift_detection; 'monitor' is the shipped rule
